newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy names new ambassador for Albania.
newsitem.headline: Italy names new ambassador for Albania.

text.p: Italy named a new ambassador to Albania on Wednesday, taking the place of a controversial envoy whose nomination was revoked only 48 hours after Rome had appointed him to take over in Tirana.
The Rome government also announced it would send more troops to a multinational force it is leading in Albania to boost security for planned June 29 elections in the Balkan state.

The Italian cabinet approved the appointment of Marcello Spatafora, 56, the serving ambassador to Australia, resolving an episode that political opponents had pounced on as an embarrassment to Italy's image in the Balkans.
Spatafora was formerly ambassador to Malaysia and Malta and organised Italy's 1990 European Union presidency.

Political commentators said that a prime concern in the appointment was that the new ambassador should be seen to be a safe pair of hands and completely removed from recent events in troubled Albania.
The present Italian ambassador, Paolo Foresti, is overdue for replacement after serving out his turn.
He was also at the centre of a controversy last month when a Tirana newspaper accused him of bias in favour of Albanian President Sali Berisha.
The paper added that he had tried to undermine the role of European mediator Franz Vranitzky.

Manfredo Inciso di Camerana, initially named as Foresti's replacement, had his appointment revoked after he was quoted by Italian daily La Repubblica as criticising Foresti and the foreign ministry in an interview.
Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said at the time that Incisa had been replaced because his comments showed he was not a suitable candidate.
Dini told reporters in the Sicilian capital Palermo earlier on Wednesday that extra Italian soldiers would be sent to Albania but would only remain there for a brief time.

"Together with Defence Minister (Beniamino) Andreatta, we are already planning a greater presence in the two weeks spanning the elections to guarantee safety in all areas where voting takes place," Dini said on the margin of a conference.
"After the elections, which we want to be free, fair and honest, the military presence will be ended swiftly," Dini said.
